header: Development split (task t22). Operation descriptions and decline thresholds are tuned against these entries; the reported numbers that matter come from held-out.json (assumption c38). Sourced from issue #30 (Needle3 POC) and issue #31 (tiny-agent middle layer) example prompts, and challenge probes s13/s16 run on the DGX Spark 2026-09-19. Grid entries (source grid-2026-09-19, ids dev-g*) cover every operation across phrasing classes (imperative, question, symptom, terse, jargon) plus should-decline classes; each carries a `class` field so the bench can report accuracy per class. Authored by the development agent in one sitting: the held-out split must come from someone else.

world.comment: The machine the expectations assume. The bench grounds against these names (not the box it runs on) unless --live is passed, so a score measures the tier, not the host.
